newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan navy to make port call to South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan navy to make port call to South Africa.

text.p: The Taiwan navy will send three vessels to South Africa for a port call, despite Pretoria's decision to switch diplomatic recognition to China, a defence ministry official said on Friday.
Two U.S. Perry-class frigates and a supply vessel will head to South Africa in March for a regular friendship port call and an international show of naval vessels, the official said.
The visit had the support of Taiwan's foreign ministry, the official, who declined to be identified, said by telephone.
Foreign Minister John Chang last month announced retaliatory measures against Pretoria, including suspension of aid projects and treaties, in protest at its decision to switch ties.
South Africa's President Nelson Mandela announced in November that his country would scrap diplomatic recognition of Taiwan by the end of this year in favour of Beijing.
South Africa was the biggest of the Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies.
China has in the past several years stepped up its efforts to isolate Taiwan internationally, wooing countries that recognise Taipei.
China has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949. Beijing has insisted that Taiwan is an inseparable part of the mainland subject to eventual reunification.
